chunks: And from him, from Faḍālah, from Ḥusayn ibn ʿUthmān, from al-Ḥasan al-Ṣayqal, from Ibn Miskān, from Abī Baṣīr, who said:
I asked him about a man and a woman praying in one house, with the woman on the right of the man beside him. He said: "No, unless there is between them a handspan or a cubit."

Then he said: "The length of the saddle of the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم was one cubit, and he would place it in front of him when he prayed so that it would screen him from anyone passing in front of him."

key_terms.بِحِذَائِهِ: directly beside him, aligned with him
key_terms.ذِرَاعٌ: a cubit as a measure of distance or height
key_terms.رَحْلِ: saddle; here, an object used as a screen in front of the one praying
key_terms.شِبْرٌ: a handspan as a measure of separation
key_terms.يَمُرُّ: passes by in front of the one praying
key_terms.يُصَلِّيَانِ: they perform salat together or at the same time

ai.seo_question: Can a man and a woman pray side by side in the same room?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling about the positioning of a man and a woman when praying in the same place, indicating that they should not stand directly side by side without some separation. It also cites the practice of the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم in placing a barrier before himself during salat, showing the importance of a physical separator in the prayer space.
